A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSW/SQW research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original shape-classification, dataset-distance, point-cloud, synthetic-texture, and functional-distance experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds synthetic digit-shape classification, classifier-accuracy correlations, and stability studies.

M1.justification: The domain projections, quantile embedding, Gaussian-process functional projections, quadrature, and Monte Carlo construction of SQW/DSW remain unchanged. The new parameter guidance and experiments concern the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST-2000, comprising noisy, randomly rotated point clouds derived from five digit classes, and evaluates relationships between MNIST dataset distances and classifier accuracy. These extend coverage within the existing shape-classification and dataset-comparison domains; previous datasets and scenarios remain.

E2.justification: Gaussian OTDD is newly evaluated alongside OTDD, s-OTDD, and DSW in Appendix C.5.1/Figure 8. Other comparator sets are retained. KID and patch-based WoW already appeared in v1's appendix; the newly discussed Busemann methods are not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 adds bidirectional 5-NN accuracy evaluation over 100 MNIST split pairs, classification checks with k=1,3,5, and systematic projection-count, grid-size, and kernel-parameter sweeps. Existing primary protocols remain. Exact projection budgets in C.5.1 are inconsistent: the prose associates S=100000 with 1000 outer times 10 inner projections, while Figure 8 labels configurations differently.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's functional-discretization and point-cloud scaling studies, v2 adds SQW/TLB correlation and parameter sensitivity on MNIST-2000, neighborhood-size and seed stability, classifier-accuracy correlations, and an 18-configuration DSW/OTDD sensitivity study. Figure 1, Tables 2–3, and Figure 8 substantially expand checks of stability and practical relevance.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes runtime reporting from single values to values with ± uncertainty terms. Appendix C.4.2 also explicitly reports a rerun with a different random initialization. Existing 1000-split and five-run reporting remains; the new timing uncertainty is not clearly defined, and an increased timing replicate count is not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the original classification accuracies but replaces runtime values; GW on FAUST-1000 changes from 187.8 to 1048.2 ± 357.3 ms without an explained setting change. New results include MNIST-2000 SQW accuracy of 84.8 ± 4.7%, a GW timeout, and the correlation and stability results in Figure 1, Figure 8, and Tables 2–3. Original plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 excludes the zero dual vector from its support condition. Propositions 3.3/A.5 also replace proportional Gaussian/spherical SW distances with exact equality, deleting v1's C_d factor. Under Equations (3)–(4) and N(0,I_d), Gaussian slicing differs by sqrt(d), so this introduces a local normalization error. The principal DSW theorem and Appendix B proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same Banach-space slicing framework, SQW/DSW construction, discretized metric-equivalence claim, and application scope. Added flow-matching and sample-complexity suggestions are future directions, not newly achieved contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations of large-grid numerical instability, degeneracy as the kernel parameter grows, small-sample limitations in choosing k, and weak classifier correlations caused by restricted accuracy variation and omitted costs. Appendix C.7.2 also explains patch-based discrimination through locality, translation robustness, and texture stationarity. These substantially expand interpretation and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit project-code link, the MNIST-2000 construction recipe, and practical guidance on selecting projection counts, grid sizes, and kernel parameters. Existing hardware, software, interpolation, and inner/outer projection implementation details are retained, with the implementation subsection relocated.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 4 expand methodological positioning through comparisons with concurrent Busemann Gaussian slicing and connections to established sliced-Wasserstein embeddings. Additional discussion connects the work to hierarchical sample complexity, flow matching, and patch-based image representations. These are substantive relationships beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main narrative and most existing prose remain intact. v2 adds explanatory definitions and proof roadmaps, clarifies SQW/DSW terminology, reorganizes Appendix C, moves the LLM disclosure to Appendix D, and updates the publication header and affiliation formatting. The added scientific sections do not constitute a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 1, 7, and 8 and Tables 2 and 3, and expands Table 1 with MNIST-2000 columns. These substantially extend the displayed experimental evidence. Existing figures are retained and renumbered, with accompanying caption and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical scrutiny through classifier-linked validation and parameter/seed sensitivity studies, while the code link and parameter guide improve reproducibility. These provide a modest net gain over v1. Benefits are tempered by inconsistent projection counts in C.5.1, unexplained Table 1 timing replacements, and the erroneous Gaussian/spherical equality in Propositions 3.3/A.5. The normalization error concerns a scaling identity and does not itself overturn the retained topological-equivalence claim.
